kurz: How a property is taxed on purchase, while it is held and on sale, from real estate transfer tax through property tax, rental income and depreciation to the ten-year period.

bloecke.md:
For tax purposes, a property is split into two parts and taxed at three points in time. The **land** does not wear out and is therefore never depreciated; the **building** wears out and is depreciated. On acquisition, real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer) is due. While the property is held, property tax (Grundsteuer) is added and, if it is let, income tax on the surplus. On sale, Section 23 EStG (Income Tax Act) may apply.

Unlike with a securities account, there is no flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) for property held as private wealth. So neither a flat rate of 25% nor a saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) applies, and no bank withholds tax. Rental income and taxable gains on sale are taxed under the normal income tax schedule of Section 32a EStG. In 2026, the marginal tax rate is 42% from a taxable income of €69,879 and 45% from €277,826. Conversely, losses from letting can be offset in full against other income, including employment income. Together, this makes property the most flexible investment asset in tax terms for private investors, but also the most error-prone.

Every figure in a property calculation must be split between land and building. Only the building share is depreciable. If the purchase price is not split, either depreciation is lost or the tax office objects to the return.

## Real estate transfer tax on purchase

Real estate transfer tax is a matter for the federal states, and its rates differ considerably from state to state. Under Section 8 GrEStG (Real Estate Transfer Tax Act), the tax base is the consideration, as a rule the notarised purchase price.

bloecke.titel: Real estate transfer tax rate by federal state, as of 2026
bloecke.unter: There are 3 percentage points between Bavaria and the states with 6.5%. With a purchase price of €400,000, this produces a difference of €12,000 that depends solely on the federal state.

bloecke.titel: Real estate transfer tax on a purchase price of €400,000

bloecke.md: Three rules have greater consequences for this tax than its amount would suggest. First, it does not count as income-related expenses (Werbungskosten). It is part of the **incidental acquisition costs (Anschaffungsnebenkosten)** and therefore goes into the basis for depreciation, but only with the share attributable to the building. It then takes effect over decades at 2% or 3% a year. Second, Section 3 GrEStG fully exempts acquisitions between spouses and between relatives in the direct line, and acquisitions with a consideration of up to €2,500 are left out entirely. Buying the flat from your parents therefore costs no real estate transfer tax, whereas buying it from your brother does. Third, movable fixtures and fittings such as a fitted kitchen, awning or sauna do not form part of the consideration if they are shown separately in the purchase contract and realistically valued. They thus reduce the tax base.

## Property tax during the holding period

The reformed valuation rules have applied since 1 January 2025. The calculation has three stages and is structured in the same way in every valuation model; only the first stage differs.

bloecke.formel: Property tax = Property tax value × Tax base rate × Municipal multiplier
bloecke.erklaerung: The property tax value (Grundsteuerwert) is determined by the tax office, the tax base rate (Steuermesszahl) is set out in Section 15 GrStG (Property Tax Act), and the multiplier (Hebesatz) is set by the municipality. Only the last stage is set by the municipality itself, and it was reset almost everywhere in 2025.
variablen: result of the valuation; income-based in the federal model, a pure area figure in Bavaria
0.31‰ for residential property, 0.34‰ for undeveloped and commercial property (Section 15 GrStG)
percentage set by the municipality, three digits nationwide
bloecke.beispiel: Illustrative calculation. Property tax value €300,000 × 0.31‰ = €93 base amount. With a multiplier of 500%, this gives €465 of property tax a year.

bloecke.titel: Consequences of the property tax reform
bloecke.md:
The reform was designed to be **revenue-neutral** at municipal level, not for the individual plot. Overall, the municipality takes in roughly the same as before, but the burden shifts between plots, in some cases considerably. Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, Hamburg, Hesse and Lower Saxony calculate with their own state models, and other states deviate in the tax base rates. Section 15 GrStG additionally reduces the base rate by 25% for residential property in social housing and for housing cooperatives, and by 10% for listed buildings.

As an operating cost item, property tax remains **recoverable from tenants**, meaning it can be passed on to them. Economically, the landlord therefore only bears it when the property is vacant. Municipalities may also levy a property tax C (Grundsteuer C) on undeveloped plots that are ready for building, in order to make speculation more expensive.

## Surplus calculation for letting

Income from letting and leasing (Einkünfte aus Vermietung und Verpachtung, Section 21 EStG) is receipts minus income-related expenses. Almost everything connected with the property is deductible: interest on debt (not the repayment), property tax, management, insurance, trips to the property, account charges, tax advice for the rental income annex (Anlage V), maintenance expenses and depreciation. The result can be negative. In the first years of a debt-financed property, a loss is the norm.

The rest of the lesson works with an example property. It is a flat of 80 m², built in 1995, with a purchase price of €400,000, incidental purchase costs of 8% (€32,000) and total acquisition costs of €432,000. According to the purchase contract, the land share is 30%, so the building share is €302,400. The loan of €250,000 costs an effective 3.97%, which is the rate Dr. Klein showed on 3 September 2026 for a ten-year fixed-rate period. The initial repayment rate is 2% and the annual basic rent €12,000.

bloecke.titel: From rent received to the tax result in the first year of letting
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation. The tax loss of around €5,000 arises entirely from tax depreciation (AfA), which is not matched by any payment. Without it, there would be a surplus of €1,030.

bloecke.titel: Tax calculation and cash calculation for the same year

bloecke.md:
Repayment is not an income-related expense. It shifts wealth from one form into another and is not an expense. A return in which the entire annuity payment is deducted is wrong.

The contribution to the owners' association's **maintenance reserve (Erhaltungsrücklage)** is not yet deductible. The amount only becomes deductible in the year in which the association spends it on a maintenance measure. The property manager's annual statement shows the contribution separately. Part of the service charge (Hausgeld) therefore only has a tax effect years later.

## Straight-line and declining-balance depreciation

Section 7(4) EStG sets out three straight-line rates. Buildings completed after 31 December 2022 are depreciated at 3% a year; for completion between 1925 and 2022, 2% applies, and for older buildings 2.5%. If an expert report proves a shorter useful life, faster depreciation is permitted. The provision expressly names 33, 50 and 40 years as benchmarks.

Since the Growth Opportunities Act (Wachstumschancengesetz), there has also been **declining-balance depreciation (degressive AfA)** under Section 7(5a) EStG. It allows 5% of the respective residual value if construction began or the purchase contract was signed between 30 September 2023 and 1 October 2029. It applies only to new residential buildings, and in the case of a purchase only if the building is acquired in the year of completion. Switching to straight-line depreciation is permitted at any time. After the switch, depreciation is based on the residual value and the remaining useful life (Section 7(5a) sentence 8 EStG). The switch only pays off once this straight-line amount is higher than the declining-balance amount. With a useful life of around 33 years, on which the 3% is based, this is the case after about 14 years. In addition, the special depreciation for new rental housing under Section 7b EStG is permitted (4 × 5%, construction cost ceiling €5,200 per m², tax base at most €4,000 per m², Efficiency House 40 with QNG seal).

bloecke.titel: Annual depreciation on a building value of €300,000, straight-line 3% and declining-balance 5%
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation. Over ten years, declining-balance depreciation gives €120,380 of depreciation, straight-line €90,000. From year 11, the declining-balance annual amount is below €9,000. A switch nevertheless only pays off after about 14 years, because straight-line depreciation is then calculated from the residual value and the remaining useful life.

bloecke.md: At a 42% marginal tax rate, the lead of €30,380 in depreciation corresponds to around €12,760 of liquidity that is available ten years earlier. However, declining-balance depreciation reduces the residual value for tax purposes more quickly. On a sale within the ten-year period, this lead is therefore taxed as a higher capital gain. In this case, the tax is only deferred, and the value of declining-balance depreciation lies in the interest advantage of this deferral. On a sale after the period has expired, by contrast, the saving is retained for good.

## Maintenance expenses or production costs

This distinction determines whether an invoice has its full effect immediately or is spread over fifty years. **Maintenance expenses (Erhaltungsaufwand)** keep the building in its existing condition, for example when an old heating system or old windows are replaced. They are fully deductible in the year of payment. For buildings held as private wealth and used mainly for residential purposes, they may also be spread evenly over two to five years under Section 82b EStDV (Income Tax Implementing Ordinance). This helps if a single large deduction would lower the marginal tax rate too much.

**Production costs (Herstellungskosten)** arise with an extension, with a substantial improvement beyond the original condition and in the easily overlooked special case of Section 6(1) no. 1a EStG.

The building share of the acquisition costs is €302,400. The limit is 15% of that, that is, €45,360 net, calculated over three years from acquisition.

- Variant A covers bathrooms and floors for €44,000 net and is therefore below the limit. The amount is deductible immediately, namely at €52,360 including VAT, because a landlord of residential property cannot deduct input VAT. At 42%, the tax effect in the first year is around €21,990.
- Variant B additionally covers the windows for €6,000 net, €50,000 in total, and is above the limit. The entire amount becomes post-acquisition renovation costs (anschaffungsnahe Herstellungskosten) and increases the depreciable basis (AfA-Bemessungsgrundlage) by €59,500 including VAT. It takes effect at 2%, that is €1,190 a year, which amounts to a tax effect of around €500 a year for fifty years.

Nominally, the same amount is deducted, but spread over half a century. The windows for €6,000 net thus shift a tax effect of around €22,000. Extensions and maintenance work that usually arise every year are not counted. VAT is only left out when checking the limit; the gross amounts are deducted.

## Ten-year period on sale

Section 23(1) sentence 1 no. 1 EStG covers sales of land if no more than ten years lie between acquisition and disposal. In both cases, the dates of the notarised purchase contracts are decisive. Handover, payment of the purchase price and entry in the land register play no role for the period. The gain is taxed at the personal tax rate; the 25% rate does not apply here. It only remains tax-free if the total gain from all private disposal transactions in the year is below €1,000. This limit is an exemption threshold (Freigrenze), not an allowance.

schritte.text: Add ten years to the date of the acquisition contract. If the sale contract is dated after that, the gain is tax-free regardless of its size.

Even within the period, the gain is tax-free if the property was used exclusively for your own residential purposes between acquisition and sale, or in the year of sale and the two preceding calendar years. The second variant does not require three full years. An uninterrupted period that extends into three calendar years is sufficient.
The gain is the sale price minus selling costs minus acquisition and production costs. Under Section 23(3) sentence 4 EStG, the acquisition costs are reduced by all depreciation claimed.
The tax is not withheld at source. It falls due with the tax assessment notice, often a year later, and triggers ongoing advance payments.

bloecke.md:
The flat is bought in 2020 for €400,000. With €32,000 of incidental costs, the acquisition costs are €432,000. Depreciation of 2% on a building value of €302,400 gives €6,048 a year, €42,336 over seven years. It is sold in 2027 for €520,000; the estate agent's costs are €10,000.

- The reduced acquisition costs are 432,000 − 42,336 = €389,664.
- The gain is 520,000 − 10,000 − 389,664 = €120,336.
- The tax at a 42% marginal tax rate is around €50,500, plus solidarity surcharge and church tax where applicable.

Without the reduction for depreciation, the gain would have been €78,000. The €42,336 of depreciation that saved tax for seven years increases the gain here in full. Three years later, after the period had expired, no tax would be due, and the saving from depreciation would be retained for good. In this example, there is a difference of around €50,500 in the after-tax result between the two dates.

The owner-occupation exception is misunderstood as “lived there for three years”. It requires uninterrupted use for your own residential purposes in the year of sale and in the two preceding years. Letting in the year of sale after moving out, on the other hand, does no harm if the owner still lived there themselves in that year (BFH, IX R 10/19). A common case is letting after moving out in an earlier year, followed by a sale. The exception then no longer applies, even after nine years of owner occupation, because the owner does not live there in the year of sale.

In addition, a home office claimed as a business expense does not serve residential purposes. The corresponding co-ownership share can therefore fall outside the exemption.

## Owner-occupied property

With an owner-occupied property, there is no depreciation, no income-related expenses and no deduction of interest on debt. The rent saved is not taxable income, but it is also not a receipt that costs could be set against. Two tax reductions remain. Under Section 35a EStG, 20% of the labour costs of tradespeople's services are deducted directly from the tax liability, up to €1,200 a year. Section 35c EStG supports energy-efficiency renovations of properties that are more than ten years old with 7% in the year of completion, 7% in the following year and 6% in the third year, up to a total of €40,000 per property. Both are deductions from the tax, not from the tax base, so they take effect regardless of the marginal tax rate. Material costs do not count under Section 35a. Cash payment rules out the deduction; an invoice and a bank transfer are required.

bloecke.titel: Letting at a reduced rent (Section 21(2) EStG)
bloecke.md:
If the flat is let to your daughter at a reduced rent, two thresholds apply for tax purposes. The benchmark is the usual local market rent including the costs recoverable from tenants:

- From 66%, the letting counts as fully remunerated. Income-related expenses remain deductible in full, although only two-thirds of the rent is paid. This is the advantage of this arrangement.
- At 50% to under 66%, the deduction depends on a forecast of the total surplus (Totalüberschussprognose). If it is negative, the deduction is reduced proportionately.
- Below 50%, the letting must be split into a remunerated and an unremunerated part. Income-related expenses are then only deductible proportionately.

The threshold must be monitored permanently. If the local rent index (Mietspiegel) rises but the agreed rent does not, a contract falls below 66% unnoticed. The rental agreement must also stand up to an arm's length comparison (Fremdvergleich). This includes a written contract, payment of the rent as agreed and no money flowing back to the landlord.

mitnehmen: Land is never depreciated, which is why every property calculation begins by splitting the purchase price into land and building.
The tax result and cash flows systematically diverge, because depreciation reduces the result without any payment, and repayment costs money without reducing the result.

On a sale within the ten-year period, depreciation only works as a deferral, because every euro depreciated increases the taxable gain under Section 23(3) sentence 4 EStG; after the period has expired, the saving is retained for good.
If the 15% limit of Section 6(1) no. 1a EStG is exceeded, the entire amount must be depreciated, not just the part above the limit.
The date of the acquisition contract plus ten years and the question of who lived in the flat in the year of sale decide whether a capital gain such as the €120,336 in the example has to be taxed.

begriffe.text: The depreciable part of the acquisition or production costs of a building. It comprises the purchase price and incidental costs, less the share for the land. Depreciation is only calculated on this amount.

Expenditure on repairs and modernisation within three years of the purchase that exceeds 15% of the building's acquisition costs, net of VAT. Under Section 6(1) no. 1a EStG, the entire amount is then capitalised and only takes effect through depreciation.

Depreciation of 5% of the respective residual value for new residential buildings under Section 7(5a) EStG if construction began or the purchase contract was signed between 30 September 2023 and 1 October 2029. Switching to straight-line depreciation is permitted.

Period of ten years between the acquisition contract and the sale contract within which the gain from selling a property is taxable at the personal tax rate under Section 23 EStG. After that, the gain is tax-free.

Intermediate figure in the calculation of property tax. It is the property tax value multiplied by the tax base rate under Section 15 GrStG (0.31 per mille for residential property). The municipality applies its multiplier to the base amount.
